value: The recursive CLI resolves an instance-addressed device -- `cairn cc.1 restart`, `cairn tester.2 status` -- instead of hard-coding instance 0, so the instance segment the three roots declare mandatory is reachable from the one surface Akien types at.

value.what: cairn-restart-cycles-the-system -- cast the same day from the same conversation; that one is the system's lifecycle, this one is how any device's instance is addressed.
cairn groundloop stop|start|restart|status -- the prior art whose watchme disposition ('none, because the ticket proved a one-time operational command set') this ticket follows and cites.
the commit that shipped cairn/devices/cc/0/bin/restart, whose header claimed this gap was 'Ticketed separately' before any ticket existed.

value.text: Measured at cast, over ~/.cairn/devices: 24 device folders (aider_shim, base, builder, bus, cairn, cc, chart, charter, codemother, disk_only, ground_loop, harbor_master, inference_domain, learning_block, librarian, press_office, skill_block, spec, sudo_relay, superclaude, tester, test_no_verb_device, trouble, verb_device), zero containing a dot -- so '.' is an unambiguous separator -- and every one holding exactly one instance folder, `0`. Both facts are falsifiable by re-running `ls ~/.cairn/devices`.

The header of cairn/devices/cc/0/bin/restart asserted this was 'Ticketed separately' before any ticket existed. This cast makes the claim true. Recorded because a comment asserting another artifact exists is a claim like any other.

Rehearsal pass 1 returned 51 gaps and one cannot_proceed, all of one shape: the ticket named the seam and never named the lines. The BUILD SPEC appended to `how` settles D1-D7 off bin/cairn's standing text -- the refusal is the bad-verb branch's own shape (bin/cairn:166-176), and the exhaustive tooth (the cannot_proceed) runs against a mirrored fixture, reading the live root only to enumerate names.
